clue.text: Lady lacking a position at work

indicators.note: lacking says the following word, a, is missing from the lady's name

parts.note: Bertha is a woman's name, so a lady can stand for it

explanation.surface: A woman finds herself without a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A berth can mean a job or post, as in finding a comfortable berth with a firm.

clue.text: Analysed as needing help by the way?

definitions.meaning: a problem analysed has been split into its parts
a car stranded at the roadside after a mechanical failure needs rescue

explanation.definitionFit: Data that is analysed is separated into parts; a vehicle that fails on the road is stuck waiting for a tow truck.

clue.text: Feel bad about impolite daughter bursting out

indicators.note: bursting out says the daughter's letter leaves the word for impolite

parts.note: impolite means rude

explanation.surface: A parent regrets a rude daughter's outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue something is to regret it, to feel sorry about it.

clue.text: Charlton is a part of London

definitions.meaning: Charlton ... was the American film actor of Ben-Hur
a district in the west London borough of Hounslow near Heathrow

explanation.surface: A claim that Charlton is a district of London, which it is (in the south-east).
explanation.walkthrough: Charlton really is a London district, so the surface reads as a plain fact; here it is the actor's first name instead.
explanation.definitionFit: The actor's surname, and the name of a west London suburb near Heathrow airport.

clue.text: Dirty article to be removed behind vehicle, black stone

indicators.note: behind puts the trimmed word for dirty after the vehicle and black

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: to be removed says the article's letters are taken out of the word for dirty

parts.note: dirty means unclean
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Instructions to clear a filthy item from behind a car, near a black stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbuncle is a red gemstone, a garnet cut in a rounded shape without facets.

clue.text: Stare, beginning to end, in game that's miserable

indicators.note: in places the altered stare inside the game's name

parts.note: chess is a board game

indicators.note: beginning to end says the first letter of the stare word moves to the back

parts.note: to leer is to stare in a nasty way

explanation.surface: Staring from start to finish at a gloomy game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to end' moves the stare word's first letter to its back before it goes 'in' the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerless describes something gloomy and joyless, a synonym for miserable.

clue.text: Final wish at Oxford maybe brings tear

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, is the wish on a gravestone
a student at a university such as Oxford is said to be up

explanation.surface: A dying student's last request causes tears.
explanation.walkthrough: British students are 'up' at university while in residence and 'go down' when they leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To rip up a document is to tear it into pieces, so the phrasal verb matches.

clue.text: Like one of the lesser players with no potential for growth

definitions.text: Like one of the lesser players
definitions.meaning: in tennis tournaments the weaker entrants are not ranked into the draw
a field or plant without seed cannot sprout

explanation.definitionFit: A tournament player not given a ranked place is not seeded; ground never sown has no seeds to grow.

clue.text: Keeping well away from heat — i.e. with this could make ice

definitions.meaning: storing goods in a refrigerated place keeps them cool

definitions.text: i.e. with this could make ice
definitions.meaning: put C, short for cold, in storage inside the letters i.e. and the result is the word ice

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is cryptic: 'cold storage' read as storing C (cold) gives I-C-E when it goes inside 'i.e.'.
explanation.definitionFit: Refrigerated keeping of food is the literal sense; the second treats the phrase as a letter instruction.

clue.text: You would get upset about theologian creating spin

indicators.note: about puts the reversed word around the theologian's letters
get upset, in a down clue, says the word for you is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: ye is the old word for you
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: Someone warns that you'd be upset by a theologian's spin on things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'would' only links; 'get upset' suits a down clue, where the word reads upward, and 'about' wraps it round the theologian's degree.
explanation.definitionFit: An eddy is a swirl of water or air spinning against the main current.

clue.text: Maybe maidens returning strip and lie a long time?

parts.note: in cricket a maiden is an over with no runs scored, so maidens are examples of overs

indicators.note: returning says the word for strip is read backwards

parts.note: to peel is to strip off a skin

explanation.surface: Young women going back to undress and lie down for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maidens' looks like young women but is a cricket term.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversleep is to stay asleep past the intended time, lying in bed too long.

clue.text: Prime bit of Stilton with smell that's foul and strong

indicators.note: the prime, or first, bit of the cheese's name is its opening letter

parts.note: olid is a rare word meaning foul-smelling

explanation.surface: A piece of Stilton cheese with a foul, powerful smell.
explanation.walkthrough: Stilton is a strong-smelling English blue cheese. OLID is an old adjective for rank-smelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Solid can mean sturdy or robust, firmly built, which is a sense of strong.

clue.text: Perth nag: horse that's excited race experts?

indicators.note: excited suggests agitation, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: An excitable racehorse from Perth, with the experts at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' looks like horse racing but means an ethnic group.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethnographers study peoples and cultures, so they are specialists in human races.

clue.text: One flying from Spooner's group that drifts around

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so this signals such an exchange

parts.note: to bum around is to wander aimlessly
a herd is a group of animals

explanation.surface: A bird escaping from a drifting flock, in the manner of Spooner.
explanation.definitionFit: The hummingbird is a tiny bird, famous for hovering flight, so it is something that flies.

clue.text: Someone making claim for product? It's averred to be false

indicators.note: false suggests something not genuine, so these letters are reworked into another order

explanation.surface: A salesman's claim for an item, which turns out to be untrue.
explanation.definitionFit: One who promotes goods in commercials makes claims about them to the public.

clue.text: Request I make to char to clean vault?

parts.words: Request I make to char to clean
parts.note: asking a cleaning lady to tidy my place, I would say '...', meaning do my house

explanation.surface: Someone asks the cleaner to clean a vault.
explanation.walkthrough: A char is a British cleaning lady; 'do' means clean, so the request is 'do me', run together.
explanation.definitionFit: A dome is a rounded vault forming a roof, as over a cathedral.

clue.text: A bit of extra time? Don't be the first to jump for joy

parts.note: people leap for joy, and to leap is to jump
one who is not first may come second

explanation.surface: Advice not to be the first to leap with happiness, in a bit of extra time.
explanation.definitionFit: A leap second is an extra second added to clocks occasionally to keep pace with Earth's rotation.

clue.text: Quiet repose with little hesitation that's grabbed by someone in church

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: grabbed says the word by is seized and held inside the preceding pieces

parts.note: repose means rest
er is a short hesitant sound

explanation.surface: Someone at church gets quiet rest, hesitating a bit.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'by' is taken literally: it is what 'that's grabbed' places inside the quiet-rest-hesitation string.
explanation.definitionFit: A presbyter is an elder or priest in certain churches, so a church office holder.

clue.text: Interrupt endlessly? Bizarrely, arousing unhealthy interest

indicators.note: bizarrely suggests oddness, so the remaining letters are rearranged
endlessly says the final letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: Constant interruptions that strangely become prurient.
explanation.walkthrough: Interrupt less its end gives INTERRUP, which 'Bizarrely' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Prurient describes an excessive or lewd interest, especially in sexual matters.

clue.text: Female employees with superb hair

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI with I for 1
tresses are long locks of hair

explanation.surface: Women staff members with gorgeous hair.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is a British term for top quality; crosswords often write the 1 as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Waitresses are women who serve tables in restaurants, so female staff.

clue.text: Garment draped around shoulders — or head

definitions.meaning: a sleeveless cloak worn over the shoulders
a headland, a point of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: Something worn on the shoulders, or on the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' seems to name a part of the body for a garment, but it is a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloak worn around the shoulders, and a promontory such as Cape Horn.

clue.text: Set of books housed in a bizarre chamber?

indicators.note: housed in puts the set of books inside the following pieces

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or bizarre
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A collection of books kept in a weird room.
explanation.definitionFit: An antrum is an anatomical cavity, such as a sinus in the skull bone.

clue.text: Stupid gent bent on crossing ring road, would you believe it!

indicators.note: crossing says the jumbled letters straddle the ring and road
stupid suggests muddle, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: a ring is O-shaped

explanation.surface: A daft man, bent on crossing a ring road; how unbelievable!
explanation.walkthrough: Gordon Bennett is a British exclamation of surprise. 'Stupid' jumbles GENT BENT ON so that its letters, 'crossing', sit either side of the ring and road.
explanation.definitionFit: This British exclamation expresses astonishment, much like 'Good heavens!' or 'Blimey!'.

clue.text: Primate in Protestant order briefly

indicators.note: briefly says the last letter is cut off

parts.note: the Orange Order is a Protestant fraternal body in Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A senior bishop within a Protestant brotherhood, for a short while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' suggests an archbishop in a church context, but it is an ape.
explanation.definitionFit: Orang is short for orang-utan, a great ape and so a primate.

clue.text: African destination not for taking in?

definitions.meaning: takeaway food is bought to eat elsewhere, not inside

explanation.walkthrough: 'taking in' looks like visiting or absorbing, but refers to eating in a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Togo is a West African nation; food sold as a takeaway is ordered 'to go'.

clue.text: Like one farm animal or another born to be disposed of

indicators.note: to be disposed of says the born letter is removed

parts.note: bovine means relating to cattle, another farm animal

explanation.surface: Choosing between two farm animals, one born to be culled.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovine means relating to sheep, just as bovine relates to cattle.

clue.text: Like the heartless taking chances —- they may go in for bad language

definitions.text: they may go in for bad language

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: heartless says the middle letter of the word is taken out

parts.note: to take chances is to run risks

explanation.surface: Cruel gamblers who are prone to swearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the H at the centre of THE, leaving TE.
explanation.definitionFit: Asterisks are used in print to stand for letters of swear words, as in f***.

clue.text: Notice ring being removed from elastic

indicators.note: being removed from says the word ring is taken out of the elastic word

parts.note: springy means elastic
taken as written

explanation.surface: A notice saying a ring is to be removed from an elastic band.
explanation.definitionFit: To spy something is to notice or catch sight of it.

clue.text: Veteran's embarrassed look, holding guns back

indicators.note: back says the whole assembly is read backwards
holding puts the guns inside the colour and the look

parts.note: an embarrassed face is red
gats is slang for guns
lo means look, as in lo and behold

explanation.surface: An old soldier blushes, cradling his guns.
explanation.walkthrough: RE(GATS)DLO is built first, then 'back' reverses all of it.
explanation.definitionFit: An old stager is someone with long experience, a seasoned old hand.

clue.text: Leader of city or county meeting Queen

parts.note: Mayo is a county in the west of Ireland
R is regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A civic head or county leader meets the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: The mayor is the elected head of a town or city council.
